scope: R6 suite execution on multiple presets and per-case preset provenance complete for CLI/MCP. Overall task 9, the expanded common-TC provenance requirements and fresh Web14 acceptance remain open.

contract.inputs: CLI --chain-presets is repeatable. MCP chainPresets accepts an array of preset IDs or JSON paths; raw inline specs use baseDir for named lookup. The same app.RunMatrix usecase is registered as test.run-matrix.
contract.cases: Movable v2 preset references/extends are replaced before lookup, preserving case overrides. Selected preset content is read once for each target and used for every case. Inline fixed declarations and v1 cases are explicitly refused as unmovable.
contract.lifecycle: All targets are prechecked before execution. Each target owns a separate ordinal workspace and session. Execution is serial; default suites stop before the next starts. An ordinary target failure preserves later results. Cleanup failure or cancellation prevents further attempts. Explicit keepUp retains owned networks.
contract.results: Selected preset IDs appear in matrix rows; resolved case preset IDs appear in CLI summaries, session.json, status.json and report.json, including skipped/blocked branches. Case override IDs remain distinct from the selected base ID.
contract.metadata: Preset names do not alter execution fingerprints or v1 migration equivalence. Legacy v1 records omit the new optional field.
contract.verdict: Both surfaces use RunMatrixOut.ExitCode: infrastructure/blocked or strict skips=2; test failures=1; otherwise=0. MCP retains JSON on isError instead of replacing per-target results with prose.
contract.planning: Composition matrix planning produces labelled plans without executing targets. Attach plans retain the existing explicit refusal.
contract.chainID: MCP chainId now matches CLI --chain-id; unsafe/fractional JSON numbers and int64 overflow fail instead of being ignored. Full-width nonnegative decimal/hex strings retain exact values.

native.intentionalFailure: WBFT preset declares 77774 while the native runtime uses 77773; the later WEMIX target still runs

storage: CLI owned node data is stopped, public diagnostics are preserved with content/mode/group/mtime, and chain rm runs before MCP starts. A 20 GiB free-space check precedes each surface. Browser evidence copies preserve SHA256, mode, uid/gid and nanosecond mtime. No referenced prior proof or user file removed.
limitations: Native CLI positive and MCP intentional-middle-failure scenarios use different WBFT declarations; identical-input CLI/MCP parity is proved by the RPC contract tests.
Matrix launching was added to CLI/MCP; existing Web history/session capture receives the additive preset IDs. This stage does not add a Web multi-target launch form.
Full common-TC provenance also asks for binary/version/fork/signing/skip context; existing artifacts hold some dimensions, but complete adequacy remains part of tasks 9 and 10.
Fresh Linux HEAD L1, remaining R3/P4/R4/R5, tasks 10–14 and frozen Web14 acceptance remain open.
